definition: The idea that all matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving; how they are arranged, how far apart they are and how they move explain the properties of solids, liquids and gases.
A measure of how hot something is: the higher the temperature, the greater the average kinetic energy of its particles.
The lowest possible temperature, $-273\ \text{°C}$ or $0\ \text{K}$, at which the particles of a substance have the least possible kinetic energy.
The force per unit area that a gas exerts on a surface, caused by its moving particles colliding with that surface.
The random, jerky movement of microscopic particles in a liquid or gas, caused by uneven collisions with the much smaller, fast-moving molecules of the liquid or gas.
The smallest particle of an element, made of a tiny central nucleus with electrons around it.
A particle made of two or more atoms joined together, such as a water molecule.
An atom, or group of atoms, that has gained or lost electrons and so carries an electric charge.
